## Summary

A plain comment on a GitHub issue now answers the factory's question. One recognition rule, `github_factory.admit_answer_notice`, serves both the signed webhook and the poll pass, then hands the comment to the answer core (`factory_questions.admit_answer`). A comment on an issue whose question round is `outstanding` or `answered` is an answer first, with or without a mention, and never also a mention revision. It must come from a `User` acting directly or through another GitHub App (not the factory's own App), whose effective permission is write, maintain or admin, on an issue a fresh App read shows open and still carrying the WorkItem's trigger label. The comment's author, App provenance, issue and creation time come from the factory's own authenticated read (the poll listing, or a comment read for a webhook). Refusals are logged by reason code and identifiers only (`answer_from_bot`, `answer_not_authorized`, `ticket_closed`, `trigger_label_absent`, and the core's outcomes). A comment that is not an answer is refused exactly as before (`ordinary_comment`, `app_authored`, `sender_mismatch`), and edits stay `unsupported_action`. The GitHub issue read now keeps the newest 1,000 comments of a longer thread.

Decisions taken where the contract left room:

1. Posting-state recovery. An answer seen while the round still reads `posting` (its question comment is on the ticket but not yet recorded `outstanding`) used to get a permanent `not_outstanding` receipt from the answer core. `_decide` now refuses it with `question_posting` before writing anything, under the WorkItem lock, so it also covers a round that moved from `answered` to a new round's `posting` after the intake looked. The intake turns that into a retry: the webhook answers 503 and the delivery audit stays `retryable`, so a redelivery of the same delivery admits it; the poll pass keeps an `answer-retry:<comment id>` cursor key and decides the comment on a later pass. The answer core's own test for the `posting` case now asserts the raise and no receipt.
2. Webhook mode has no poll pass and GitHub never redelivers a 503 by itself, so a deferred webhook answer also records an `answer-retry:<comment id>` key in the scope's poll cursor, added atomically. The poll pass drains those keys in poll mode. In webhook mode a new work item reconciler step, `drain_answer_retries`, drains them on every tick, independent of the label sweep's interval, and costs one query when no key is held. The poll pass never writes or drops these keys when it saves its own cursor, so a key a webhook adds during a poll pass survives it. The step is declared in the telemetry step domain.
3. A Slack kickoff WorkItem has no trigger label and no label removal cancels it (#5380), so only the open check applies to answers on it; refusing them would strand a kickoff run's questions, whose comment tells the reporter to answer plainly. A closed issue still refuses. A reviewer read decision 3 as requiring a label here; this is left for the maintainer.
4. As for a mention, an answer is refused `binding_missing` when the WorkItem's agent no longer has a GitHub surface on the repository and `installation_mismatch` when it arrives from another installation. A comment that already has an answer receipt replays before any other check and any GitHub read, so a mention that answered is never admitted again as a mention after its round clears, and a poll pass interrupted by its deadline re-reads admitted answers cheaply. On an issue with an open round, the poll pass skips any comment it lists with an `updated_at` later than its `created_at`, or created before its listing threshold, so an edit never becomes an answer, even one made before the pass first saw the comment (a facts request edited into plain text), matching the webhook's `unsupported_action`. A body the facts exchange accepts on the authenticated read is never an answer. A comment edited within the cursor's own second is skipped too, while a new reply created in that second is still read. In personal mode an answer on a WorkItem the owner did not start is refused before any GitHub read, as a mention would be.
6. Rolling upgrade. While an older API replica still serves, a plain answer that reaches it is refused there as an ordinary comment, as today, and is not read again; the person answers again or mentions the App. The answer core's guard (`test_factory_question_mixed_version.py`) now lists the intake as a reader of the round state, and a new case proves that an answer reaching a new replica after an older replica settled the asker is the round's one continuation. Recovering answers an older replica dropped would need a backfill read of the issue after the roll; not built, recorded here for the maintainer.
5. Issue read order. Decision 9 says "the 10 pages ending at the last page", which for a thread whose last page is partial returns fewer than 1,000 comments; acceptance criterion 8 requires the newest 1,000. The read follows the criterion: it reads one earlier page when the last page is partial and keeps the newest 1,000 (at most 12 comment page requests, counting page 1). A `rel="next"` without a `rel="last"` is followed forward as before within ten pages and refused as unavailable beyond them. `IssueContent.comments_truncated` is renamed `earlier_comments_omitted`; its one reader writes `_Earlier comments were not read._` after the description, and `_Later comments were not read._` is no longer written.

## Verification

Local checks:

1. Every acceptance criterion's command from the issue, run against a disposable Postgres and Valkey: `uv run pytest apps/api/tests/test_github_answer_intake.py -q` (56 passed) and `uv run pytest apps/api/tests/test_github_issue_read_order.py -q`.
2. Criterion 9 regression set plus `test_factory_answer_admission.py`, `test_factory_question_mixed_version.py`, the reconciler suites (`test_factory_label_reconcile.py`, `test_workitem_reconciler.py`, `test_factory_intake_notices.py`, `test_factory_multi_repo.py`, `test_requester_instruction_admission.py`) and the telemetry package tests, after merging the current `next`: all pass. `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy`, `uv run lint-imports` and the test-time ratchets pass.
3. Revert checks. With the intake sources reverted (`github_factory.py`, `github_factory_events.py`, `factory_poll_intake.py`, `factory_questions.py`), all 42 intake tests fail on assertions. With only the `_decide` change reverted, both `test_posting_window_answer_is_admitted_once` cases and the core's `posting` case fail (the posting delivery records `not_outstanding`, the poll pass keeps no retry key). With the read order change reverted, the 1,250 and 1,300 comment cases fail while the 3 and 1,000 comment cases pass both ways.
4. Review fixes, each failing with its source fix reverted: `test_posting_window_answer_is_admitted_by_the_reconciler`, `test_dedupe_mention_answer_after_the_round_clears` (both orders), `test_refused_edit_after_permission_granted`, `test_facts_body_on_the_authenticated_read_is_never_an_answer`, `test_refused_binding_missing`, `test_refused_installation_mismatch`, `test_a_next_only_listing_is_followed_forward_and_returned_whole`. `test_refused_payload_claims_another_author` pins that the authenticated read, not the payload, grants authority (passes both ways). Round 2 fixes, each failing on an assertion with this round's sources reverted: `test_posting_window_answer_is_admitted_by_the_reconciler_tick`, `test_posting_window_webhook_key_survives_a_concurrent_poll_pass`, `test_refused_edit_at_the_cursor_boundary`, `test_refused_retained_service_item_in_personal_mode` (both doors). Final round: `test_refused_comment_edited_before_the_first_poll` fails with the poll fix reverted, and the poll case of `test_refused_edited_comment` now expects no receipt, as the webhook writes none. `test_boundary_reply_in_the_cursor_second_is_new` and `test_posting_window_answer_edited_into_facts_is_never_an_answer` pass both ways, as liveness and regression pins.
5. The immediate and late cases run on both paths with real numeric comment ids: a reply in the question comment's own second with the next id admits one request; an older comment delivered after the question admits none.

Each test drives the production caller: signed `POST /github/webhook` deliveries or a real poll pass, with the question posted through the questions route by the real GitHub tracker into the GitHub fake. The GitHub fields relied on (`issue_comment` action, `performed_via_github_app`, `user.type`, issue `state`, the comments listing `Link` header) are cited to GitHub's REST and webhook documentation in the tests.

Live or external proof CI cannot produce: none run here; left open under the discovery waiver above.

## Summary

A plain answer to the factory's questions now restarts the factory on every non-GitHub tracker. `Tracker.poll_marked` takes a required `answering` keyword (no default, every adapter and caller migrated). On an answering issue, Jira Cloud, GitLab, the memory tracker and the GitHub port turn every new human comment, mention or not, into a `Disposition.ANSWER` notice carrying the comment's creation time. `verify_current` holds an answer only while the issue keeps the trigger label, is open (Jira status category not done, GitLab and memory not closed) and the comment still stands. The shared intake (`factory_tracker_intake.py`) builds the answering set from the question rows (`posting`, `outstanding`, `answered`), checks the answerer's start authority with `may_start_with` at admission time, and hands each answer to `factory_questions.admit_answer` with the bare tracker comment id and its creation time, so the fence orders by ids on Jira and GitLab. An answer seen while its question row still reads `posting` (the question comment can already be on the ticket) is held like a deferral, with no hold comment, and admitted on a later poll once the row is `outstanding`, instead of being recorded as a permanent `not_outstanding` refusal. Jira and GitLab `read_ticket` now keep the newest 100 comments, rendered oldest first after `_Earlier comments were not read._`; at 100 or fewer the output is unchanged and the Jira golden file is byte-identical.

## Related issue

Closes #5789

Realizes ADR 0286 decision 6 on the non-GitHub trackers. Part of #5783. The GitHub production intake and the GitHub issue read order are #5787; here `forges/github/tracker.py` changes only the `poll_marked` signature and its answer notices (decision 8).

## Verification

Local checks:

1. `uv run pytest apps/api/tests/test_factory_tracker_answer_intake.py apps/api/tests/test_factory_tracker_intake.py apps/api/tests/test_factory_tracker_intake_auth_log.py apps/api/tests/forges apps/api/tests/test_factory_poll_intake.py apps/api/tests/test_factory_answer_admission.py apps/api/tests/test_factory_rediscovery_bitbucket_cloud.py apps/api/tests/test_factory_question_mixed_version.py apps/api/tests/test_requester_instruction_admission.py apps/api/tests/test_personal_execution_admission.py -q` against disposable Postgres and Valkey at the current head: 2194 passed, 185 skipped (the skips need a live GitLab fixture).
2. The other suites that use the in-memory tracker, the Jira fake or the shared intake (`test_factory_ci`, `test_factory_merge_notice`, `test_factory_questions_route`, `test_factory_rediscovery`, `test_factory_status_comment`, `test_factory_tracker_result_admission`, `test_factory_tracker_results`, `test_factory_triage_handoff`, `test_forge_credential_health`, `test_personal_execution_admission`, `test_publication_closing_reference`, `test_workitem_dispatch`, `test_work_item_issue_read`, `test_requester_instruction_admission`, `test_factory_question_ending`): 889 passed.
3. `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run mypy` no issues.
4. Revert checks. With the intake change reverted, 15 behaviour tests in `test_factory_tracker_answer_intake.py` fail on their request and receipt assertions and the 4 pure refusal cases pass both ways. With the adapters' answer logic disabled but the signature kept, every ANSWER test in the contract vector, `test_jira_poll.py` and `test_gitlab_core_units.py` fails on its assertions and the 3 liveness and regression cases pass. With the posting hold disabled the posting test fails on a `not_outstanding` receipt; with `note:<id>` passed instead of the bare note id the GitLab fence test fails.

Acceptance criteria:

1. AC1 and AC2: `apps/api/tests/forges/contract/test_plain_answer.py` runs on every port-driven harness (`memory`, `memory-minimal`, `jira-github`, `gitlab`, `memory-tracker+bitbucket-cloud`, `memory-tracker+bitbucket-dc`); one test asserts that set equals every contract harness id except `github`. On each, after the factory posts its question through the port, a plain comment by an authorized writer is exactly one current `ANSWER` notice in one poll, by that writer, with a zoned creation time and a comment id the answer fence orders after the question; without `answering` it is no notice and a repoll does not repeat it. The contract harnesses carry no database, so the request half of the outcome (exactly one new request on the same WorkItem in one poll pass) is proven through the real intake pass with Postgres in `test_factory_tracker_answer_intake.py` on Jira, GitLab and the memory tracker (criteria 3 to 6 and 9 below). This is how the criterion was read, and the coordinator accepted it after review round 2: the contract vector proves the notice on every harness, and the Postgres intake tests prove the request.
2. AC3 `-k refused`: zero requests for an outsider, the bot, an `app` account, an issue whose trigger label was removed, and an issue with no outstanding question, each paired with an admitting liveness answer. For the removed label, the same poll pass also processes the removal, which cancels the WorkItem and deletes its round, so the test asserts zero requests, no receipt and the round gone rather than the round still outstanding.
3. AC4 `-k closed_before_delivery`: Jira done, GitLab closed and memory closed, each with an open liveness twin that admits one request. On Jira the done issue leaves the labelled search, and the poll that follows the comment also processes the done cancellation; the test asserts no cancellation was processed before that poll.
4. AC5 `-k authority`, AC6 `-k "coalesce or follow_up"`, AC7 `test_jira_poll.py -k answer`, AC8 `-k read_ticket` (Jira 130 and 100 comments, the golden, GitLab 130 and 100 notes), AC9 `-k answer` (GitLab units and the memory tracker through the real intake).
5. Posting recovery `-k posting`: the Jira fake applies the question comment and loses the response, the round stays `posting`, a person answers, the poll writes no receipt and no hold comment and keeps the cursor; the run retries the question route, the round becomes `outstanding`, and the next poll admits exactly one request.
6. Comment id and time `-k fence`: a Jira answer in the question's own second with a higher id, and a GitLab note in the question note's own second, are admitted, which works only when the bare id and the creation time reach `admit_answer`.

7. Review round 1 fixes. A comment's kind is decided at admission under the WorkItem lock: a mention on a WorkItem whose round is `posting`, `outstanding` or `answered` goes to the answer core, and a comment that already has an answer receipt starts nothing more (`-k "answer and mention"`: a GitLab reply that mentions the bot on a two-label binding starts one request; a mention replayed after its round cleared starts nothing). A Jira or GitLab first poll, which repeats while a held page leaves the label's cursor unsaved, delivers an answering issue's comments as answers (`test_answer_first_poll_again_after_a_held_page_admits_the_answer`, plus adapter units). Each fails with its fix reverted.
8. Mixed versions (#5842's round-state guard now lists this intake): `test_factory_question_mixed_version.py::test_an_answer_to_a_posting_round_is_held_until_the_redrive` drives the real Jira intake. A round left `posting` by a lost tracker response, whose asker an older replica then settled, holds the answer without a receipt or hold comment until the reconciler's re-drive clears the round; the cursor then moves on.
9. AC10 regression command: `apps/api/tests/forges/test_offline_lifecycle.py`, named in the issue, was deleted on next by 82d446fcf before this change, so the command runs the remaining paths unchanged, plus `ruff check .` and `mypy`.

10. Review round 2 fixes. A mention promoted to the answer core is first verified as an answer under the WorkItem's trigger label, so it starts nothing once the issue is closed or has lost that label, even when another label's poll delivers it before the trigger label's poll processes the cancellation (`test_answer_mention_on_an_earlier_labels_poll_needs_the_open_labelled_issue`, GitLab, closed, unlabelled and an open liveness case). An answer whose round left `posting`, `outstanding` and `answered` after the poll's snapshot is held like a posting one, with no receipt, so the next poll's snapshot delivers a reply that mentions the bot as a mention and it starts one request (`test_answer_snapshot_taken_before_the_round_cleared_keeps_a_fresh_mention`, Jira; the Jira fake gains a one-shot hook that lets the answer's run end between the snapshot and the search). Each fails with its fix reverted; the open liveness case passes both ways.
11. Final review fixes. A Jira or GitLab first poll, which a label whose first page held an issue repeats, now delivers a running issue's mentions made since its label was last added instead of only remembering them, so a reply held on such a poll is delivered on the replay and is not recorded as seen before it is admitted (`test_answer_snapshot_stale_on_a_first_poll_delivers_the_held_mention_on_jira` and `..._on_gitlab`; the GitLab fake gains a one-shot hook beside the Jira one). Every mention, answer or revision, now acts only while the issue is open and keeps the WorkItem's trigger label, checked in the intake on every tracker, so a held reply replayed after the issue closed or lost that label starts nothing before the cancellation (`test_answer_held_reply_replayed_after_the_issue_changed_on_gitlab`, closed, unlabelled and an open liveness case; Jira's own mention check already reads the label and status category). Each fails with its fix reverted; the open case passes both ways.

Known limits, not fixed here:

1. During a rolling upgrade, a replica built before this change can hold the intake lock; its adapters have no answering set, so a plain answer it polls past is not seen again. The window is the roll itself, and only plain comments made during it are affected; a mention still admits a revision.
2. In the mixed-version case above, the re-drive clears a round that was never recorded as posted, so an answer to that question starts nothing. That is the re-drive's existing rule for such a round.
3. A plain (no mention) answer can be lost for good when it is read under an answering snapshot taken before its question was posted. Trigger: the question and the plain reply both land after the poll took its snapshot and before the adapter reads the issue's comments. On Jira the next poll delivers it. On a GitLab first poll (no saved cursor for the label) the adapter records the note as seen without a notice, so once the cursor saves it is skipped. The memory tracker's cursor likewise moves past a filtered plain comment. The window is the time between one poll's snapshot and its comment read, and on GitLab only while the label has no saved cursor. The person has to comment again. Left for a later true-up.

External API shapes (Jira comment listing order and paging, `accountType`, status category, comment delete; GitLab notes sort) are proven against the in-repo fakes, whose payloads follow the providers' REST references cited in the new tests.
